sources.entry: Dive into Claude Code by VILA-Lab - A research-lab systematic analysis of the Claude Code codebase whose headline finding — overwhelmingly infrastructure rather than model — reframes Claude Code as a harness.

summary.one_liner: A research-lab source-level architectural analysis of Claude Code (v2.1.88), arguing that most of its codebase is deterministic harness infrastructure rather than AI decision logic, plus a design guide for agent builders and cross-system comparisons.
summary.what_it_does: The repository presents a written analysis of Claude Code's internals, covering the agentic query loop, the permission and safety system, extensibility (hooks, skills, plugins, MCP), context and memory with CLAUDE.md layering and compaction stages, subagent delegation, and session persistence. It states a headline split of roughly 1.6% AI decision logic versus 98.4% deterministic infrastructure. It also maps 5 human values to 13 design principles and links each to implementation choices. Beyond the Claude Code analysis, it includes a design guide for building agents, a comparison table with OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent, and a curated catalog of official Anthropic posts, docs, community reimplementations, security research, and academic papers. The README points to docs/architecture.md and docs/build-your-own-agent.md for full detail, and much of the later material is dated changelog and release-note commentary.
use_cases: Understanding how Claude Code's agent loop and permission system work internally
Designing permission gates, context compaction, or recovery logic for a new coding agent
Comparing coding-agent architectures such as Claude Code, OpenClaw, and Hermes-Agent
Finding curated research papers and blog posts on AI agent harness design
Reviewing security considerations such as pre-trust windows and approval fatigue in agent tools
notable: Claims 98.4% of Claude Code's codebase is deterministic infrastructure, with only 1.6% AI decision logic
Maps 5 human values through 13 design principles to concrete implementation choices
Cross-system comparison table of Claude Code, OpenClaw, and Hermes-Agent across six design dimensions
Curated catalog of Anthropic docs, community reimplementations, security research, and papers organized by design question
Documents pre-trust execution window CVEs and the 50-subcommand approval fallback in the legacy parser
caveats: Architecture sections describe the v2.1.88 snapshot; later Claude Code releases may differ
Much of the content is an analysis document and reading guide rather than runnable software; no install steps are given
Some later claims (such as release notes and newer model behavior) are reported from sources the README itself describes as recent and not independently replicated
